questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement multi-tenant zero-trust mTLS using SPIFFE IDs, short-lived cert rotation, and KMS-backed CA in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE trust domains per tenant
- CSR-based certificate rotation with short lifetimes
- Per-tenant mesh policies (Istio/OPA) for north-south and east-west traffic
- Workload identity verification via SPIFFE IDs

## Code Example
```yaml
# CSR bootstrap (outline)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-td1-csr
spec:
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-clientSigner
  request: <base64-csr>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Per-tenant policy (outline)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-td1-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://td1/ns/default/sa/gateway"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET","POST"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle cert revocation in case of a compromised gateway?
- How would you test cross-tenant isolation under peak load?

- Fluent Bit routing per-namespace
- NamespaceConfigMap as policy store

```yaml
# NamespaceConfigMap example
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: tenant-logging-config
  namespace: tenant-a
data:
  tenantID: "tenant-a"
  sinkURL: "http://log-sink-a:24224"
```

```yaml
# sidecar snippet concept (pseudo, for illustration)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: cnf-logging-sidecar
spec:
  containers:
  - name: sidecar
    image: cnf/sidecar:latest
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: tenant-logging-config
```

```bash
# minimal validation

```

- How would you audit cross-tenant log access?

## Why This Is Asked
CNF reliability hinges on runtime trust alongside image provenance. This question tests practical knowledge of in-cluster attestation, trust roots, and controlled upgrades across clouds.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime attestation, KMS-backed keys, central attestation service
- Image provenance and policy enforcement against a root of trust
- Canary upgrades and per-CNF rollback in multi-namespace/multi-cloud
- Minimal in-namespace validation and rollout gating

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example policy (illustrative)
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-attestation
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: attestation-check
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["CNFDeployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Attestation must be present and signed"
      pattern:
        metadata.attestationSigned: true
```

```yaml
# Attestation report (illustrative)
attestation:
  signer: "kms://arn:aws:kms:..."

```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle attestation revocation and key rotation without downtime?
- What are the failure modes if the central attestation service is unavailable, and how would you mitigate them?

## Why This Is Asked
Assesses ability to design tenant-isolated feature flagging and traffic-splitting at the CNF edge with CRDs and sidecar routing, including rollback and observability.

## Key Concepts
- per-tenant traffic shaping; CRD-backed policy; stable hash routing; zero-downtime rollout; observability and rollback.

## Code Example
```yaml
# CRD
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: tenantcanaries.example.org
spec:
  group: example.org
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              tenantID:
                type: string
              canaryPercent:
                type: integer
              canaryService:
                type: string
              prodService:
                type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: tenantcanaries
    singular: tenantcanary
    kind: TenantCanary
```

```go
// Pseudo code: sidecar decision
tenant := getHeader(X_TENANT_ID)
pathHash := hash(req.path)
if (pathHash % 100) < canaryPercent(tenant) {
  route = canaryService
} else {
  route = prodService
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you implement idempotent canary progress across restarts?
- How would you monitor per-tenant canary health and automate rollback?
